stage: HISTORIE (engine stage 6) - fractal axis + competing frames - cache
disputedNote: Even where this story begins is disputed - picking a start date is itself a position. Frames change emphasis and annotation, never the record.

frames.label: Jun 2026 Lancet letter
frames.note: This is the frame the Lancet signatories and Maktoob coverage open with. Under this start, the story is health professionals citing documented harms in Gaza and asking the World Medical Association to apply existing membership rules to the Israeli Medical Association. It reads as a profession-internal accountability question.

frames.label: Oct 2023 attack and war
frames.note: This is the frame the Israeli Medical Association and Jerusalem Post coverage open with. Under this start, the story is a wartime boycott campaign aimed at a national medical body whose country was attacked on Oct 7, with the IMA calling the proposal a weaponization of medicine. It reads as politicization of a clinical institution during active conflict.

frames.label: 2010s boycott wave
frames.note: This is the frame longtime boycott-movement observers and Forward coverage on individual targeting open with. Under this start, the story is the latest step in a longer boycott trajectory that has moved from institutions toward individuals across academia, culture and now medicine. It reads as continuity with prior BDS-era debates rather than a new event.

bands.label: Lancet letter and IMA pushback
bands.summary: Over 1,150 health professionals signed a Lancet-published letter on Jun 16 demanding IMA suspension from the WMA, and the Israeli Medical Association publicly denounced the proposal days later.

nodes.title: Open letter in The Lancet calls for IMA suspension from World Medical Association
nodes.what: An open letter published in The Lancet and signed by more than 1,150 health professionals, academics and medical organizations asked the World Medical Association to suspend the Israeli Medical Association over alleged complicity in harms to the health system in Gaza. Signatories pointed to documented attacks on hospitals and clinicians and invoked existing WMA membership criteria as the basis for action.
nodes.disputed: Maktoob and the letter's signatories describe it as health professionals applying long-standing WMA conduct rules to documented wartime harms; the Israeli Medical Association and Jerusalem Post coverage describe the same letter as a politicized boycott campaign aimed at a national medical body during active conflict.

nodes.title: Israeli Medical Association denounces the proposed boycott
nodes.what: The Israeli Medical Association issued a public rejection of the Lancet letter, telling Jerusalem Post that the proposal sought to expel a national medical body in the middle of a war started by an attack on its country. The IMA framed the call as an attempt to use the World Medical Association's institutional machinery against Israeli clinicians.

nodes.title: Jerusalem Post opinion column argues medicine must not be weaponized
nodes.what: A Jerusalem Post op-ed published the same day argued that international medical bodies should not be turned into venues for boycott campaigns targeting Israel, and warned that admitting political criteria into WMA membership decisions would erode professional norms. The piece functioned as an editorial complement to the IMA's institutional statement.

bands.label: Gaza war and medical mobilization
bands.summary: The Oct 7 attack and the subsequent Gaza war drove sustained public-health and medical-professional debate over Israeli institutional responsibility and over hospital and clinician harm in Gaza.

nodes.title: Hamas-led attack on southern Israel
nodes.what: Hamas and allied Palestinian armed groups launched a large cross-border assault from Gaza on communities and a music festival in southern Israel, killing roughly 1,200 people and taking about 250 hostages according to Israeli authorities. Israel declared war the same day and began large-scale military operations against Gaza. The event reshaped subsequent debates over medical institutions, hospitals and professional bodies on both sides.

nodes.title: Israeli raid on Al-Shifa Hospital
nodes.what: Israeli forces entered Al-Shifa Hospital, Gaza's largest medical complex, saying Hamas operated a command infrastructure beneath the site. Israeli officials presented the operation as targeting militant use of medical facilities, while Palestinian health authorities and international agencies described patients, staff and displaced civilians trapped inside under severe conditions. The raid became a central reference point in subsequent disputes over hospital protection under international humanitarian law.
nodes.disputed: The Israeli military describes the operation as a precise action against Hamas military use of a hospital; Palestinian health authorities and UN agencies describe it as an assault on a functioning hospital that endangered patients and staff.

nodes.title: ICJ provisional measures order in South Africa v Israel
nodes.what: The International Court of Justice ordered provisional measures in the genocide case brought by South Africa against Israel, requiring Israel to prevent acts within the scope of the Genocide Convention and to ensure humanitarian assistance reached Gaza. Israel rejected the underlying allegation while saying it would comply with its legal obligations. The order became a recurring citation in medical and public-health appeals about Israeli institutional responsibility.

nodes.title: ICC arrest warrants against Israeli and Hamas leaders
nodes.what: Pre-Trial Chamber I of the International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defence minister Yoav Gallant, and against a Hamas commander, in connection with alleged crimes in Gaza and the Oct 7 attack. Israel rejected the warrants and said the court lacked jurisdiction. The warrants intensified arguments inside medical associations about whether engagement with state-linked institutions was sustainable.

bands.label: BDS pressure and boycott debates
bands.summary: Academic, cultural and professional boycott campaigns targeting Israeli institutions expanded through the 2010s, setting precedents and vocabulary that later medical-association proposals draw on.

nodes.title: American Studies Association votes to boycott Israeli academic institutions
nodes.what: The American Studies Association membership endorsed a resolution honoring the Palestinian civil society call for an academic boycott of Israeli universities. The vote made the ASA the largest US scholarly association at the time to take such a position. The resolution targeted institutional ties rather than individual scholars.
nodes.disputed: ASA proponents described the vote as professional solidarity with Palestinian academic freedom under occupation; opponents, including more than 200 university presidents and the American Association of University Professors, described it as discrimination singling out one nation's scholars.

nodes.title: Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.) votes to divest from companies tied to Israeli occupation
nodes.what: At its general assembly, the Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.) voted by a narrow margin to divest roughly 21 million dollars in holdings from Caterpillar, Hewlett-Packard and Motorola Solutions over uses of their products in the occupied Palestinian territories. The decision came after years of denomination-internal debate and study committee reports.
nodes.disputed: Church proponents described the vote as a targeted stance against the occupation that was not a boycott of Israel; Jewish organizations and Israeli officials described the move as aligning a mainline denomination with the BDS movement and singling out Israel.

nodes.title: US states begin passing anti-BDS legislation
nodes.what: Starting in 2015 and accelerating through 2016, US state legislatures passed laws restricting state contracts with or investments in entities that boycott Israel. By the late 2010s more than half of US states had adopted some form of anti-BDS measure, typically requiring contractor certifications or pension fund divestment from listed companies.
nodes.disputed: Supporters described the statutes as anti-discrimination measures targeting commercial boycotts; civil liberties groups including the ACLU described them as restricting constitutionally protected political speech and challenged several in federal court.

nodes.title: Airbnb announces removal of West Bank settlement listings
nodes.what: Airbnb announced it would delist about 200 rentals located in Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, citing the contested status of the territory under international law. The company faced lawsuits from Israeli hosts and US-based plaintiffs and reversed the policy in April 2019 after litigation and political pressure.
nodes.disputed: Human rights groups described the original announcement as conforming with longstanding international concerns over settlement commerce; Israeli officials and settler residents described it as discriminatory and aligned with boycott politics, and several US states moved to place Airbnb on divestment lists.

nodes.title: Ben and Jerry's announces ending sales in Israeli-occupied territories
nodes.what: The ice cream brand Ben and Jerry's, owned by Unilever, said it would not renew its license to sell in Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories when its arrangement expired in 2022, while continuing to sell inside Israel. Unilever later in 2022 transferred the Israeli business to a local licensee, and the brand's independent board sued its parent over the move.
nodes.disputed: The brand's independent board described the decision as inconsistent with selling product in occupied territories rather than a boycott of Israel; Israeli officials and US state governments described it as a boycott of Israel and triggered divestment actions under state anti-BDS statutes.

nodes.title: Middle East Studies Association endorses academic boycott resolution
nodes.what: Members of the Middle East Studies Association of North America voted by a wide margin to endorse the Palestinian call for an academic boycott of Israeli institutions. The vote followed years of internal debate and added one of the field's main scholarly bodies to the list of US associations that had passed similar resolutions over the prior decade.
nodes.disputed: Proponents inside MESA described the vote as solidarity with Palestinian colleagues working under occupation; opponents inside and outside the association described it as politicizing scholarship and singling out Israeli institutions for exclusion.
